normalize_email strips and lower-cases. It raises ValueError for no-@ and for two @ (count != 1), and for 'a@localhost' because the domain regex requires a dotted name. tests/test_normalize.py:16 asserts the exact expected output. Line 19 parametrizes 'no-at-sign', 'a@b@c.com' and 'a@localhost' (plus extras) with pytest.raises(ValueError). I ran the test file and 26 passed.

normalize_phone in cottonwood/normalize.py strips to digits and returns +1 plus 10 digits for US inputs. It keeps the country code for +44 numbers (8-15 digits). It raises ValueError for 7-digit '555-0134' and for '+12', which is a +1 number without 11 digits. tests/test_normalize.py parametrizes all four US formats (plus 8015550134) and expects '+18015550134'. It asserts '+44 20 7183 8750' gives '+442071838750'. It asserts ValueError for '555-0134' and '+12' (and others). pytest on tests/test_normalize.py: 26 passed.

The domain case goes through the parametrized test_domain_is_bare_host at line 52-53.
